_meta.description: Closing segment of the demo video (tech + future, <= 60 s): the GitHub repo's architecture and Meta models, the pipeline that keeps taking in records, then three planned directions. Shots t* in tools/demo/walkthrough.mjs; vision scenes in tools/demo/vision.html.

segments.text: Now, under the hood. It's all open on GitHub, with the architecture in our README.
Official records come in with zero model calls. Then Muse Spark does the reading.
Here's a real one. Muse Spark finds the stance in a committee report, keeps the exact sentence, and scores it, and our validator checks the quote word for word.
That's over twenty thousand quotes. It turns 765 bills into plain yes-or-no questions, finds the conditions behind votes, and audits itself, re-scoring quotes blind to catch bias.
A person approves every draft, a contract gate checks every deploy, and Muse Code built much of the site.
Here's where it goes next. Any public source can feed the same pipeline: hearings, floor speeches, press releases, public Facebook and Instagram posts, even decades of past Congresses.
So when a politician says something new, their position updates, with the quote attached. And Meta's multilingual models let every voter read it in their own language.
One Congress today. Informed voters everywhere tomorrow. Come explore, and see the proof for yourself.
